sections.title: The letters gn
paragraphs: The letters gn sound like /n/ in (gnat) /næt/, which is a tiny fly. This letter group makes only one sound. The first letter is silent. You hear only the regular nasal sound of the second letter. This pairing appears at the start of a few words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Keep the sides of your tongue against your side teeth. Let the air flow freely out through your nose. Turn your voice on so your vocal cords vibrate. Place a finger on your nose to feel the buzz.

sections.title: When to use it
paragraphs: At the beginning of words before a vowel, the letters gn always make the sound /n/. You can hear this in (gnat) /næt/. The first letter is a silent letter, as you also hear in (gnaw) /nɔː/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not try to say the first letter. Learners often try to make a hard sound at the start. Start directly with the tip of your tongue behind your teeth. Say the sound smoothly, just as you start the word net.
